headline: President Bush designated the African Union as an international organization eligible for certain legal privileges and immunities in the United States.
what_it_does: This order names the African Union as a public international organization under US law. That status lets the organization and its officials receive certain privileges, exemptions, and immunities, such as protections from some lawsuits and some tax exemptions. The title does not list exactly which protections apply or whether any are limited.

who_it_affects.group: The African Union and its staff working in the United States
who_it_affects.how: They become eligible for legal protections and exemptions given to recognized international organizations.

who_it_affects.group: People or businesses with legal claims against the African Union in the US
who_it_affects.how: They may face limits on bringing certain lawsuits or legal actions against the organization.
